items.prompt: One single continuous take from a locked-off side-on camera at adult eye height about eight metres away: no cuts, no scene change, no close-up, no zoom, the framing never changes. On an early-spring Hokkaido forest trail, a Japanese woman in her mid 40s in a maroon field jacket, charcoal trousers and dark hair tied in a low bun walks from left to right facing forward, never turning her head toward the camera, her face never visible. Behind her on the left, an adult brown bear on all fours bursts out of the bamboo, jaws wrenched wide open with fangs bared, ears pinned flat, the fur along its neck bristled, closes the gap in two powerful bounds and lunges onto her back from behind, knocking her forward toward the ground. Captured up to the moment of impact only, nothing beyond it. Nothing red and nothing stained. Both the woman and the bear stay in the same side-on frame the whole time. 6 seconds. Photorealistic, shot on RED camera. Documentary style.
